verdictNotes: The `cut` design is the right one and it is better than the shape I proposed in round 1. I reproduced the author's counter-evidence exactly: my "record offers as heard only after confirm" shape, applied to the 59c1fa72 consumer under the new tests, fails 3 of 43 hostProjection rows (with the head's CF-H3 store, 2 of 43), because a campaign frame arriving inside the re-armed window clears it and the next offer then settles behind the cut one, stalling the chain again. Round 1's `probe-fixshape.log` covered only the quiet-remount case; I withdraw the claim that the shape "recovers the case". The cut predicate (`live && settling > 0` at dispose) is exact for every ordering a shipped mount can produce: a disposed binding never confirms, so an unfinished step at dispose is precisely an offer nobody will ever confirm. My probes found one latent spurious-fire class (a dispose scheduled as a microtask after a successful `confirm` but before the trailing `.then(() => settling -= 1)` runs; PROBE-S1 reproduces it with a hooked confirm) that no shipped mount can reach (projection preserves `coopSession`, `store` is a stable StoreApi, and both mounts are unconditional on projected state); its cost would be one healthy socket closed and a rejoin from EMPTY, never a certification. It is carried with a one-line hardening and a pin (CF-H14). The same-tick dispose boundary (consume then unmount before the queued step starts) is handled correctly but unpinned (R2-M2 survived; PROBE-S2 is the pin; CF-H15). CF-H3's "not behind" is sound: a lineage ahead of the cursor is only possible through frames the fold's own ordering guard would reject, and PROBE-H3a shows it continues inside that span and starts fresh past it; the one conflation (a sequenced frame the fold rejected while mounted also reads as "behind", PROBE-H3b) is safe-side and equals pre-G1 behaviour. Nothing blocks merge.

verdictNotesRound1: The notes are real. My probes found that G1's design moves, rather than closes, a liveness hole in dormant receipt-mode code: (1) a host that unmounts while an offer's guarded refresh is awaited comes back onto the continued lineage with no quiet window (the heard mark is written at consume, before the step completes), nobody ever confirms that offer, and the transport then withholds every later ACK behind it; F recovered this case through the window or the EMPTY-fold failure, G1 recovers it only at pending overflow (64 offers). (2) The single-slot store forgets campaign A's lineage when campaign B claims, so returning to A on its still-registered transport gets a fresh EMPTY cell while the per-transport heard mark skips the window; the next linked offer then fails `adjunct-failed` and rejoins, so this one self-heals at the cost of one failed receipt. (3) The store continues a lineage that missed frames during an unmount gap and re-projects it at bind, so a stale balance can show for up to one window. None of the three certifies anything the view did not apply, sends anything new on the wire, or is reachable before P2CG1G2 binds a creator and P2CG1H installs the port; (1) must be closed by the consumer's next owner before activation, and the fix shape (record the heard cursor when the step completes, not when the frame arrives) passes every registered pin. Five of my ten mutants survived: two real coverage gaps (the unbound-transport reset and the legacy-server variant of the CF-G3 case), one store/consumer predicate-drift probe, two near-equivalents. Documentary: the red receipt records Node v24.15.0 while the local receipt, the PR body and G1-PREP say v22.22.0; the behaviour text names neither the remount re-projection nor the cursor-watermark refinement of "already delivered a campaign frame". Nothing blocks merge; the activation-blocking item is carried with a concrete fix and pin.

authority.verdict: PASS (no defect; every residual withholds or restarts ACKs and never advances one)
authority.round1Finding: **Authority.** The fold cell is cached view state; receipts remain the transport's. A continued lineage cannot certify more than it applied: the disposed binding never confirms (settle returns on `!live` after its await), the remount confirms only what it folded, and the transport withholds any ACK behind an unapplied pending offer (C3, PROBE-A `acks [v1-r0]`). A replacement transport cannot inherit a stale lineage (RM-G2 caught), another campaign cannot read the first campaign's facts (C2), and a fresh cell is a new object the old binding's `fold` reference does not point at. `refusalFromFrame` keeps application errors out of the refusal posture (RM-G8 caught). The direction of every residual is safe-side: ACKs are withheld, never advanced.
authority.round2Finding: **Authority.** A cut can only cause a rejoin; it never advances a receipt. The disposed binding still confirms nothing (every `settle` path re-checks `live` before `confirm`), the remount on a cut transport confirms nothing on the dead chain (PROBE-A: confirms `[v1-r0]`, acks `[v1-r0]`), and the replacement view starts from EMPTY and is applied and ACKed on its own socket (PROBE-S3: hydration input EMPTY, acks `[v2-r0]`, balance 600000). The direction of every residual is unchanged from round 1: ACKs withheld or restarted, never advanced.

privacy.verdict: PASS (no defect; nothing new reaches the wire)
privacy.round1Finding: **Privacy.** Nothing new reaches the wire: the host join still quotes -1 (omitted), the store serialises nothing, the heard map holds integers keyed by transport identity (WeakMap, GC-bound; RM-G6 shows string keying would leak the mark across transports on one match). The re-projection writes only the local campaign store.
privacy.round2Finding: **Privacy.** The cut set holds transport identities only (WeakSet, GC-bound, never serialised); the rejoin sends the same `CampaignJoin` F sends on a fresh socket (host still quotes -1, omitted). Nothing new reaches the wire. The receipt's claim of no wire change holds.

replay.verdict: PASS at the merged head (round 1 CF-H1 closed before merge, CF-H3 closed; CF-H2 open and self-healing; RM-G9 survives as CF-H6)
replay.round1Finding: **Replay.** Offers still settle in receipt order on one queue; `foldCampaignEvent` rejects `sequence <= lastSequence` but accepts a gap, so a lineage that missed frames during a gap folds the next offer over an incomplete state (CF-H3) while the transport's prefix discipline keeps the ACK withheld. The heard mark is recorded at consume, before the step completes, so a consumed-but-unconfirmed offer leaves the record equal to the cursor and the remount skips the window (CF-H1). The single-slot store and the per-transport heard mark are keyed differently, so a lineage that never folded a frame can skip the window (CF-H2; PROBE-B). A duplicate or lower-sequence frame during a gap moves neither `lastSeq` nor the record, which is consistent (the fold would have rejected it).
replay.round2Finding: **Replay.** Receipt order is preserved: the cut chain is abandoned whole (the transport is closed with its pending list), and the replacement adopts its baseline at -1 and restarts the chain. The cut marking does not touch `heardAt`, so CF-G3's window semantics are unchanged (the window decision is made before the cut check; rejoin clears whatever was armed). Against a legacy server the surface folds campaign frames synchronously and nothing settles, so a bound legacy binding is never cut (by construction; RM-G9-rerun still survives, see CF-H6).

idempotency.verdict: PASS (no defect; RM-G4 survives as CF-H5)
idempotency.round1Finding: **Idempotency.** `claimCampaignHostFold` is idempotent for the same binding (same cell, `continued` true, re-projection is a pure overwrite); StrictMode double effects claim, dispose, claim and arm one window. `heard()`/`dispose`/`rejoin` keep F's once-only guards (CF-G8 pins the timer trade). RM-G4 survived: the store mirrors the consumer's `active` predicate by hand; if either side changes, they drift silently.
idempotency.round2Finding: **Idempotency.** Double dispose: the second sees `live === false` and marks nothing. StrictMode mount/cleanup/mount: no offer has been consumed at mount, so `settling` is 0 and nothing is cut. A cut transport bound twice: the first active bind rejoins and closes it; the stored connect never hands out an unregistered transport, so a second active bind cannot see it (PROBE-S4: a second remount while the held refresh is still pending rejoins at once, the third remount binds the replacement and is not cut). The set is never cleared, but every member is a closed transport reachable only through `held.transport` until the next host claim (CF-H13, unchanged).

concurrency.verdict: PASS (no defect; latent spurious-cut class unreachable from shipped mounts carried as CF-H14; R2-M2 same-tick pin carried as CF-H15)
concurrency.round1Finding: **Concurrency.** `held` is mutated synchronously inside the effect; the consumer writes `binding.fold.current` only in the synchronous part of `settle` before its await, so a dispose (React cleanup, a separate task) cannot interleave with that write; after the await only reads happen. The transport sets `lastSeq` before dispatch and `consume` runs inside that dispatch, so the record is exact. Liveness: a rebind on a heard transport arms no window, so the only recovery paths for a cut settle are the server's own view failure (none timed; the server never waits for an ACK, it just keeps publishing), the transport's confirmation timer (armed only after an ACK is sent, which the withheld prefix prevents), `pending-overflow` at 64 offers, or a reload. The store holds a strong reference to the last transport (one object, replaced at the next host claim); the heard map holds none.
concurrency.round2Finding: **Concurrency.** `settling` is mutated on task boundaries only (consume runs inside the transport's synchronous dispatch; the decrement is a microtask after the step). A dispose is a React cleanup, i.e. a task or a sync-lane microtask flush, so the only interleaving hazard is a dispose scheduled as a microtask between a successful `confirm` and the trailing decrement. That is the spurious-fire class below. The "miss" direction is closed: the predicate is evaluated at dispose, the increment precedes any yield, and R2-M3 (release the count when the step starts) is caught by all three CF-H1 rows.

cutDesign.mechanics: Mechanics at the head: `settling` counts offers an active binding has consumed whose step chain has not finished (incremented synchronously at consume, decremented in a trailing `.then` after `settle` resolves or `rejoin` ran). `dispose` adds the transport to a module `WeakSet` when `live && settling > 0`. `bind` on an active binding calls `rejoin()` at once when the transport is in the set (after the quiet-window decision; `rejoin` clears the window). `rejoin` closes the transport, which unregisters it, so the next effect run connects a fresh transport that is not in the set.
cutDesign.spuriousFire: **Can it fire spuriously?** Healthy settle: no (the decrement microtasks drain before any task can dispose). Dispose during the awaited refresh: correct fire (the resumed step returns on `!live`). Same-tick dispose after consume, before the step starts: correct fire (PROBE-S2: refresh never called, acks withheld at `[v1-r0]`, the remount rejoins). The one spurious class: a dispose in a microtask after `confirm` returned and before the trailing decrement; PROBE-S1 hooks `confirmApplied` to unmount in `Promise.resolve().then` once v1-r1 is confirmed, and the remount rejoins (socket 0 closed) although `acks(0) == [v1-r0, v1-r1]`. In production this ordering needs a React update committed during `project()`/`confirm()` whose sync-lane flush unmounts the surface; the dashboard mount is unconditional, the shell mount keys on the route, `projectAuthoritativeStateOntoCampaign` spreads the campaign and preserves `coopSession` (so the effect deps `campaignId/coopMode/roomCode/matchId` are stable), and `store` is the singleton StoreApi. Not reachable today; latent for any future mount gated on projected state. Hardening (one-line class): release the count synchronously at the point the step can no longer confirm or has confirmed (e.g. decrement inside `settle` immediately before `confirm` and on each early return, or keep a precise "consumed and unconfirmed" count) and drop the trailing `.then`. Pin: PROBE-S1's shape (CF-H14).
cutDesign.miss: **Can it miss?** No ordering found. Dispose before the step starts, during the await, or after a failed confirm are all covered (the last rejoins on its own). An inactive binding (`!active`) returns `isOffer(message)` without settling, so an offer it swallows is unconfirmed and uncut; that is F-era code on a transport bound to a different campaign than the mounted one, which the host connect cannot currently refuse because it passes no `expectedCampaignId` (CF-H16, a G2 design requirement, not a G1 regression).
cutDesign.interactions: **Interactions.** CF-G3 cursor-record skip: unaffected (cut check follows the window decision; both gap rows still pass; the AM1/AM3/RM-G5/RM-G6 classes are untouched). F's window: a cut remount skips straight to rejoin; the replacement arms its own window as every fresh transport does, so when the server stays quiet the CF-G4 cycle continues (PROBE-A and PROBE-S4 reach three sockets by 2T; CF-H7 unchanged). Replacement transports: new objects, never in the set (PROBE-S3). Memory: WeakSet plus one integer per binding closure; the strong reference that keeps a cut transport alive is the store's `held.transport`, bounded to one (CF-H13).
cutDesign.displayAtCutRemount: **Display at a cut remount (PROBE-RP).** `claimCampaignHostFold` runs before `bindApplication`, so a cut remount is `continued` and re-projects the retained fold (750000: the cut offer's state, which the disposed binding folded before its await) for the instant before the rejoin's replacement baseline lands. The server published that offer, so the value shown is the server's state; display-only, transient, nothing certified (CF-H17, optional).

notBehind.rule: `continues` now requires `lineage.cell.current.lastSequence >= transport.lastSeq()`. The transport cursor moves on every `CampaignSnapshot`/`CampaignEvent` with a wire event (`Math.max`), whether or not the fold accepted it. The fold's cursor moves only on accepted frames and can be adopted ahead of the wire sequence (a legacy baseline at `sequence: -1` adopts at 0 while the cursor stays -1; a sequenced snapshot adopts at `payload.revision` when present).
cases: **Behind (the CF-H3 case).** A frame during an unmount gap moves the cursor past the lineage: not continued, no re-show, fresh cell (pinned; R2-M7 off-by-one caught by that row; MH3 caught).

**Ahead.** Only reachable through frames the fold's own ordering guard would reject (`foldCampaignEvent` refuses `sequence <= lastSequence`; `foldCampaignSnapshot` refuses an older adoption). PROBE-H3a: a snapshot at wire sequence 2 with revision 10 adopts at 10 (cursor 2); a gap frame at 7 leaves it continued (re-show 640000, correct: the fold would have rejected 7); a gap frame at 11 makes it fresh (loaded record 1000000). Equality would refuse every legacy-baseline lineage (the control row; MH4 and R2-M6 caught), so "not behind" is the right predicate. I found no lineage ahead of the transport that should not continue.

**Conflation (note, not a defect).** A sequenced frame the fold rejected while mounted (PROBE-H3b: an unparseable snapshot at sequence 3 on a bound legacy stream) also leaves the lineage "behind", so the next remount gets a fresh cell and no re-show (balance 1000000 instead of the held 640000). Safe-side and identical to pre-G1 behaviour (every bind started at EMPTY); in receipt mode such a frame is `fold-rejected` and already forces recovery. Recorded under CF-H3's closure, no action.

judgments: **Retained fold re-shown at remount (accept, with a guard).** Projecting the continued fold at bind is the right symmetry with the guest (`projectMirrorToCampaign()` at bind) and is what makes R2 observable; without it the dashboard would show the reloaded record until the next frame. It is safe when the lineage is current. It is wrong when the lineage missed frames during the gap: `continues` does not compare `cell.current.lastSequence` with `transport.lastSeq()`, so a lineage behind the cursor is continued, re-shown (stale balance), and then folds the next offer over the gap; the window re-arms (the gap row pins that) and ends it within T, and the ACK stays withheld, so nothing is certified. Accept the design; add the cursor equality to `continues` (or skip the re-projection when behind) when the store next opens (CF-H3).

**Heard semantics (sound choice; wrong moment).** The cursor-watermark refinement is strictly better than the stop-report WeakSet (the author's M1 and my RM-G5 show the second gap row discriminates), and the two gap rows pin exactly what #2236 review note 2 asked. The remaining defect is *when* the record is written: at consume, i.e. when the frame reaches a binding, not when its handling completes. For a legacy frame those coincide; for an offer they do not, and an unmount between consume and confirm leaves a record that says "heard" for an offer nobody confirmed. F had no such state because every bind started from EMPTY and armed a window. The fix is local to the consumer (record non-offers at consume, offers after a successful `confirm`, using the cursor captured at consume), passes all 100 registered cases and my probes, and keeps the legacy-server behaviour the amendment wanted. It is a consumer-leaf change, which G1 owns only for CF-G3; the lane is closing, so it is carried as CF-H1 with activation as the deadline. If the owner prefers it inside G1, it must land as a new red-first commit pair and be re-reviewed on the new head.

items.round1Wording: **CF-H1 (cut settle leaves a heard mark; receipt chain stalls) [next owner of useCampaignApplicationConsumer.ts, at or before P2CG1H; must be closed before activation].** `consume` writes `heardAt` when a campaign frame reaches an active binding, before `settle` completes. A host that unmounts while an offer's guarded refresh is awaited (C3's shape) comes back onto the continued lineage with the record equal to the cursor, arms no window, and nobody ever confirms that offer; the transport then withholds every later ACK behind it (`drain` -> `prefix-pending`) while the server keeps publishing, and the view recovers only at `pending-overflow` (64 offers) or a reload. Under F the window or the EMPTY-fold `adjunct-failed` rejoin recovered it within T. Fix shape (verified: all 100 registered cases and the probe pass): record non-offer campaign frames at consume, record offers only after `confirm` returns neither refused nor recovery-required, using the cursor captured at consume. Pin under fake timers in hostProjection: baseline applied, linked offer with a held refresh, unmount, remount, release -> window re-armed, rejoin at T, no ACK past the held one, replacement view from EMPTY.
